worldbuilding.geography: Valdris: gold, harbours, strategic position — kept intact as perfect vassal, keeps its flag. Vestalia: empire of the far EAST.
worldbuilding.culture_and_society: Vestalia: women hold institutional power, meritocracy by exam never inherited. Men: soldiers, craftsmen, husbands; never judges or priests. Lara's values: Discipline, Love, Tradition, Maternal Authority. Title: Supreme Mother.
worldbuilding.history: Valdris's first queen dies suddenly (poisoned by Mirela, then a lady-in-waiting). The king marries Mirela and dies on the front 2 years ago — officially heroic; in truth Mirela paid mercenaries to withdraw his guard. Leah, daughter of the first marriage, is marginalised for 8 years.
worldbuilding.rules_and_laws: Vestalia: everything belongs to the Crown-Mother (Public 99%); perform, rise or fall. Main punishment: ritual spanking applied publicly by priestesses of Vohra — maternal correction, never sexual. After vassalage: available, not mandatory.
worldbuilding.technology_level: Middling level with military accents: state academies, logistics for large armies, harbours and mines.
worldbuilding.magic_system: The ritual fire of the Daughters of Flame and the Mother's two faces — Azara who warms, Vohra who burns. Rare magic, mostly symbolic.
worldbuilding.key_locations: Valdris Castle; Lower City; Red Velvet Inn (later Vestalian info asset); Varnholt's NORTHERN border; academies of the Daughters of Flame; harbours of Valdris.
worldbuilding.important_organizations: Daughters of Flame (raised from 6, each ~20 Valdris soldiers; '1 million' is propaganda); Vestalian women's council (Mira, Vela envoys ch5); priestesses of Vohra; exiled nobles (resistance).
worldbuilding.religions_and_beliefs: One Unique Mother, two faces: Azara the Good (light, love, order, truth; warming fire) and Vohra the Bad (same goddess, harsh face: darkness, punishment, burning fire; ritual hairbrush in right hand; not a devil). Day to Azara, night to Vohra.
worldbuilding.economy: Vestalia Public 99%: mines, land, brothels, workshops, banks — all state-owned; army fights for Mother not money. Valdris moves to planned model after vassalage.
worldbuilding.conflicts: Vestalia's conquest of Valdris; Mirela's dethroning with murder evidence; exiled nobles' resistance (old nobility, not commoners); Leah's dependence-vs-independence war; Lara's test: can she let go.
worldbuilding.relevant_data: Vestalian values: Unitary 64, Autocracy 81, Security 68, Assimilation 61, Pacifist 31, Nationalist 77, Public 99, Planning 57, Globalism 70, Religious 53, Traditionalist 83, Technology 58.
